title: Rudy
tagline: Never give up. Never skip dessert.
about: A working-class kid from a steel town chases his dream of playing football for Notre Dame.
cue: Serve the main when Rudy works at the steel mill with his dad and brothers.
faces: Serve the main when Rudy works at the steel mill with his dad and brothers.

    StartersJoliet steel mill meatloaf sandwichesSliced meatloaf with cheddar, pickles and relish on toasted breadHow to make it500g beef mince1 onion1 egg40g breadcrumbs1 tsp Worcestershire sauce3 tbsp tomato sauce1 tbsp brown sugar8 slices of white bread4 slices of cheddar1 jar of dill pickles1 jar of tomato relishMix the mince, grated onion, egg, breadcrumbs, Worcestershire and salt.Press into a lined loaf tin and spread with tomato sauce mixed with brown sugar.Bake at 180°C.Cool completely, then slice thickly.Toast the bread.Fill with the meatloaf, cheddar, pickles and tomato relish and cut in half.Notre Dame tailgate beer bratsBratwurst simmered in lager, grilled, with beer onions and mustardHow to make it8 bratwursts375ml lager2 onions20g butter8 bread rolls1 jar of wholegrain mustardSlice the onions.Simmer the bratwurst in lager with the onions and butter.Lift out the brats and grill, turning, until charred.Keep boiling the onions until the liquid reduces and they turn sticky.Toast the rolls.Fill with a brat and a pile of beer onions and finish with wholegrain mustard.MainsRuettiger family Sunday pot roastSlow-cooked chuck roast with carrots, potatoes and horseradish sour creamHow to make it1.5kg chuck roast2 tbsp vegetable oil2 onions3 garlic cloves2 tbsp tomato paste500ml beef stock1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce1 bunch of thyme2 bay leaves4 carrots800g potatoes1 tbsp cornflour150g sour cream2 tbsp horseradish cream1 crusty loafSeason the chuck roast and quarter the onions, peel the carrots and halve the potatoes.Brown the roast all over in oil in a heavy pot.Add the onions, garlic, tomato paste, stock, Worcestershire, thyme and bay leaves.Cover and cook at 160°C.Add the carrots and potatoes.Cook for another hour.Thicken the juices with cornflour.Mix the sour cream with horseradish cream.Serve the roast and vegetables with the sour cream mix and the crusty loaf, torn, to mop up the juices.Holy Cross Friday fish fryFriday nights at Holy Cross, waiting on Notre DameHow to make it600g flathead fillets150g plain flour250ml cold lager1 tsp baking powder1 L vegetable oil1kg frozen thick chips150g mayonnaise2 tbsp capers2 gherkins1 lemon300g white cabbage1 carrotBake the chips at 220°C for 25 minutes.Mix the mayonnaise with chopped capers, gherkins and a squeeze of lemon for the tartare. Toss the shredded cabbage and grated carrot with 2 tbsp of it.Whisk 120g of the flour with the baking powder and lager until smooth.Heat the oil to 180°C. Dust the fish in the rest of the flour, dip in the batter and fry in batches for 4 minutes until golden.Serve with the chips, tartare, slaw and lemon wedges.SweetsSouth Bend apple crumbleCinnamon Granny Smith apples under a buttery crumbleHow to make it6 Granny Smith apples60g caster sugar1 tsp ground cinnamon1 lemon100g butter100g plain flour60g rolled oats80g brown sugar50g pecans600ml vanilla custardPeel and slice the apples and toss with sugar, cinnamon and lemon juice.Tip into a baking dish.Rub the cold butter into the flour, then stir in the oats, brown sugar and chopped pecans.Scatter over the apples.Bake at 180°C until golden.Warm the custard and serve alongside.DrinksGolden Dome hot spiced ciderHot apple cider with maple, cinnamon, clove and orangeHow to make it1.2 L cloudy apple juice2 tbsp maple syrup6 cinnamon sticks6 cloves1 star anise1 orangePour the apple juice into a saucepan with maple syrup, cinnamon sticks, cloves, star anise and sliced orange.Heat gently without boiling.Strain into mugs and add a cinnamon stick and orange slice to each.
